chapter_title: Information and Communication Technology: World and Bangladesh Perspective

questions.question: Who is considered the pioneer of the 'Global Village' concept?
questions.explanation: Canadian philosopher Marshall McLuhan introduced the concept of the 'Global Village' in his books 'The Gutenberg Galaxy' (1962) and 'Understanding Media' (1964).

questions.question: Which of the following is the fundamental backbone for establishing a Global Village?
questions.explanation: Internet connectivity and telecommunication infrastructure provide the real-time global connectivity necessary to link people worldwide into a single interconnected community.

questions.question: Which component is NOT one of the primary elements of the Global Village?
questions.explanation: The core elements of a Global Village are hardware, software, network connectivity, data/information, and human capacity.

questions.question: How has the Global Village concept most directly transformed employment opportunities?

options.label: A
options.text: By mandating physical relocation to industrial cities

options.label: B
options.text: By enabling remote freelancing and global outsourcing

options.label: C
options.text: By eliminating electronic communication in commerce

options.label: D
options.text: By restricting job applications to domestic companies

questions.correct_answer_text: By enabling remote freelancing and global outsourcing
questions.explanation: The Global Village allows skilled professionals to work remotely for employers across the globe through online freelancing and outsourcing platforms.

questions.question: Which service delivers medical diagnosis and treatment consultation to patients in remote areas using telecommunications?
questions.explanation: Telemedicine uses telecommunication technology and ICT devices to provide healthcare services and clinical advice across physical distances.

questions.question: Which hardware device is essential for experiencing an immersive 3D visual environment in Virtual Reality?
questions.explanation: A Head-Mounted Display (HMD) provides stereo screens in front of the eyes to create a realistic three-dimensional simulated environment for Virtual Reality.

questions.question: What is the primary role of sensory data gloves in Virtual Reality systems?

options.label: A
options.text: To capture hand gestures and provide tactile feedback

options.label: B
options.text: To protect hands from electrical voltage

questions.correct_answer_text: To capture hand gestures and provide tactile feedback
questions.explanation: Sensory data gloves track hand and finger movements and provide haptic or tactile feedback so users can manipulate virtual objects.

questions.question: In military and aerospace training, what is the main advantage of using VR flight simulators?

options.label: A
options.text: It completely replaces the need for actual aircraft maintenance

options.label: B
options.text: It offers risk-free training for dangerous flight maneuvers

questions.correct_answer_text: It offers risk-free training for dangerous flight maneuvers
questions.explanation: Flight simulators allow pilot trainees to practice critical emergency responses and complex maneuvers without risking life, aircraft, or fuel.

questions.question: How does Augmented Reality (AR) fundamentally differ from Virtual Reality (VR)?

options.label: A
options.text: AR replaces the real world entirely, while VR does not

options.label: B
options.text: AR overlays digital computer graphics onto the real environment

options.label: C
options.text: AR does not use any digital technology

options.label: D
options.text: VR can only be accessed using audio headphones

questions.correct_answer_text: AR overlays digital computer graphics onto the real environment
questions.explanation: Augmented Reality enhances the user's perception of reality by superimposing digital imagery and data onto the physical world, whereas VR immerses the user in an entirely artificial world.

questions.question: Which of the following is a potential negative side effect of prolonged Virtual Reality usage?
questions.explanation: Extensive immersion in VR can cause simulator sickness (cyber sickness), dizziness, eye strain, and disorientation due to sensory mismatch.

questions.question: Who first coined the term 'Artificial Intelligence' at the Dartmouth Conference in 1956?
questions.explanation: John McCarthy proposed the term 'Artificial Intelligence' in 1956 at the Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence.

questions.question: Which two core components constitute an Expert System in Artificial Intelligence?
questions.explanation: An expert system consists of a knowledge base (domain facts and rules) and an inference engine (logical processing rules to deduce answers).

questions.question: Which programming language was historically developed specifically for Artificial Intelligence research?
questions.explanation: LISP (List Processing), created by John McCarthy, became the pioneering and widely adopted programming language for AI and symbolic computation.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the famous 'Turing Test'?

options.label: A
options.text: To determine whether a machine can exhibit human-equivalent intelligent behavior

options.label: B
options.text: To calculate the clock speed of a microprocessor

options.label: C
options.text: To evaluate the storage density of semiconductor memory

options.label: D
options.text: To detect computer hardware manufacturing defects

questions.correct_answer_text: To determine whether a machine can exhibit human-equivalent intelligent behavior
questions.explanation: Devised by Alan Turing in 1950, the Turing Test evaluates whether an artificial system can generate natural language responses indistinguishable from a human.

questions.question: Which technology enables computers to understand, interpret, and manipulate human languages?
questions.explanation: Natural Language Processing (NLP) is a branch of AI that gives machines the ability to read, understand, and derive meaning from human languages.

questions.question: Who coined the word 'Robotics' and formulated the famous Three Laws of Robotics?
questions.explanation: Isaac Asimov introduced the term 'Robotics' in his science fiction stories and formulated the Three Laws of Robotics in 1942.

questions.question: What is the function of an actuator in a robotic system?

options.label: A
options.text: To convert energy into physical motion or movement

options.label: D
options.text: To display status messages on an LCD

questions.correct_answer_text: To convert energy into physical motion or movement
questions.explanation: Actuators act like the muscles of a robot, converting electrical, pneumatic, or hydraulic energy into mechanical motion.

questions.question: The tool or gripper attached to the end of a robotic manipulator arm is called the:
questions.explanation: An end-effector is the peripheral device at the tip of a robotic arm that interacts with the work environment, such as a welding torch or gripper.

questions.question: Which industrial sector relies most heavily on automated robotic arms for precision spot welding and painting?
questions.explanation: Automotive assembly lines utilize industrial robots for high-precision repetitive tasks like welding, spray painting, and heavy component placement.

questions.question: Which robotic sensor is commonly used to measure distance and detect obstacles via sound waves?
questions.explanation: Ultrasonic sensors emit high-frequency sound waves and calculate the time taken for the echo to return to measure distance to an obstacle.

questions.question: What is the fundamental working principle of cryosurgery?

options.label: A
options.text: Destroying abnormal tissue by applying extreme localized cold

options.label: B
options.text: Burning abnormal tissue using high-frequency ultrasound waves

options.label: C
options.text: Removing tumors through mechanical laser cutting only

options.label: D
options.text: Disintegrating kidney stones through electromagnetic shockwaves

questions.correct_answer_text: Destroying abnormal tissue by applying extreme localized cold
questions.explanation: Cryosurgery uses freezing temperatures to freeze and destroy diseased or abnormal cellular tissue while preserving adjacent healthy tissue.

questions.question: Which substance is most commonly used as a cryogen in cryosurgical procedures?
questions.explanation: Liquid nitrogen, which boils at -196 °C (-320 °F), is the most widely utilized cryogenic agent for freezing abnormal cellular structures.

questions.question: The hollow needle-like instrument through which freezing agents are circulated in cryosurgery is called a:
questions.explanation: A cryoprobe is an insulated surgical probe through which liquid nitrogen or argon gas is delivered directly into the targeted tumor.

questions.question: Which cooling gas is paired with helium gas in modern cryosurgery systems for controlled freezing and thawing cycles?
questions.explanation: Modern cryosurgery systems often use high-pressure argon gas for rapid freezing to -186 °C and helium gas for controlled warming and thawing.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key clinical advantage of cryosurgery over traditional open surgery?

options.label: A
options.text: Minimal blood loss and faster postoperative recovery

options.label: B
options.text: Complete absence of any imaging guidance

options.label: D
options.text: Ability to operate without patient consent

questions.correct_answer_text: Minimal blood loss and faster postoperative recovery
questions.explanation: Cryosurgery is minimally invasive, causes little bleeding, reduces pain, and requires a significantly shorter recovery period than traditional open surgery.

questions.question: Which of the following is categorized under behavioral biometrics?
questions.explanation: Voice recognition, keystroke dynamics, and signature verification are behavioral biometric characteristics, whereas fingerprints and iris patterns are physiological.

questions.question: Which biometric technique evaluates the unique patterns of blood vessels located at the back of the human eye?
questions.explanation: Retina scanning maps the unique capillary blood vessel pattern at the back of the eye, offering extremely high security.

questions.question: Which physiological biometric feature is most widely used for national electronic ID cards (NID) and mobile SIM registration in Bangladesh?
questions.explanation: Fingerprint verification is cost-effective, fast, and universally deployed in Bangladesh for National ID card verification and biometric SIM card registration.

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of Iris recognition over Fingerprint recognition?

options.label: A
options.text: Iris patterns remain stable and unaffected by physical aging or manual wear

options.label: B
options.text: Iris scanning requires physical touch contact with the sensor lens

options.label: C
options.text: Iris recognition operates without using any digital cameras

options.label: D
options.text: Iris scanning can be spoofed easily with printed paper photos

questions.correct_answer_text: Iris patterns remain stable and unaffected by physical aging or manual wear
questions.explanation: The human iris is internal and protected by the cornea, keeping its intricate texture stable throughout life without suffering wear like fingerprints.

questions.question: Measuring the rhythm, typing speed, and dwell time of a person typing on a keyboard is known as:
questions.explanation: Keystroke dynamics analyzes the habitual timing and rhythm with which an individual types characters on a keyboard as a behavioral biometric.

questions.question: What is the primary definition of Bioinformatics?

options.label: A
options.text: Application of computer science and statistics to analyze complex biological data

options.label: B
options.text: Production of electronic circuit boards using biological enzymes

options.label: C
options.text: Cultivation of agricultural crops inside computer server rooms

options.label: D
options.text: Manual chemical titration of laboratory organic samples

questions.correct_answer_text: Application of computer science and statistics to analyze complex biological data
questions.explanation: Bioinformatics combines computer science, mathematics, and molecular biology to manage, interpret, and model biological databases like DNA and protein sequences.

questions.question: Which enzyme acts as 'molecular scissors' to cut DNA at specific nucleotide sequences in Genetic Engineering?
questions.explanation: Restriction endonucleases cleave DNA molecules at specific palindromic recognition sites, functioning as molecular scissors in recombinant DNA technology.

questions.question: What is the main function of the enzyme DNA Ligase in recombinant DNA technology?

options.label: A
options.text: To join two DNA fragments by forming phosphodiester bonds

options.label: B
options.text: To transcribe RNA back into complementary DNA

options.label: C
options.text: To split plasmid circular rings into pieces

options.label: D
options.text: To dissolve the nuclear membrane of host cells

questions.correct_answer_text: To join two DNA fragments by forming phosphodiester bonds
questions.explanation: DNA ligase acts as molecular glue, joining cut ends of DNA strands together during the creation of recombinant DNA plasmids.

questions.question: Small circular double-stranded DNA molecules in bacteria used as gene transfer vehicles are called:
questions.explanation: Bacterial plasmids are extrachromosomal circular DNA elements widely utilized as cloning vectors to carry foreign genes into host organisms.

questions.question: Which of the following is a major practical achievement of Genetic Engineering in medicine?

options.label: A
options.text: Commercial production of recombinant human insulin using E. coli bacteria

options.label: B
options.text: Elimination of computer motherboard silicon shortages

options.label: C
options.text: Invention of optical storage compact discs

options.label: D
options.text: Replacement of wireless radio spectrum with enzymes

questions.correct_answer_text: Commercial production of recombinant human insulin using E. coli bacteria
questions.explanation: Recombinant DNA technology allows engineered bacteria to mass-produce human insulin (Humulin), transforming diabetes management worldwide.

questions.question: One nanometer is equal to what fraction of a meter?
questions.explanation: One nanometer (1 nm) equals one-billionth of a meter, or 10^-9 meters.

questions.question: Nanotechnology generally deals with matter and structures sized within what dimension range?
questions.explanation: Nanotechnology involves the engineering of functional systems and materials at the molecular scale, typically between 1 and 100 nanometers.

questions.question: Who delivered the historic 1959 lecture 'There's Plenty of Room at the Bottom', laying theoretical foundations for nanotechnology?
questions.explanation: Physicist Richard Feynman envisioned manipulating individual atoms and molecules in his 1959 American Physical Society lecture 'There's Plenty of Room at the Bottom'.

questions.question: Which cylindrical allotrope of carbon exhibits extraordinary tensile strength and electrical conductivity in nanotechnology?
questions.explanation: Carbon nanotubes are seamless cylinders of graphene sheets possessing outstanding mechanical strength, thermal conductivity, and electronic properties.

questions.question: In medical science, what is a promising application of nanoscale smart particles?

options.label: A
options.text: Targeted drug delivery directly to cancerous tumor cells

options.label: B
options.text: Replacement of the central nervous system with copper wire

options.label: C
options.text: Conversion of red blood cells into plastic polymers

options.label: D
options.text: Manual extraction of DNA from living bone marrow

questions.correct_answer_text: Targeted drug delivery directly to cancerous tumor cells
questions.explanation: Nanoparticles can be engineered to carry chemotherapy drugs directly to cancer cells, sparing healthy cells and minimizing adverse side effects.

questions.question: An online auction website where individual citizens sell used products directly to other consumers represents which e-commerce model?
questions.explanation: Consumer-to-Consumer (C2C) e-commerce facilitates transactions between private individuals via a third-party online marketplace or platform.

questions.question: Which cloud computing model provides virtualized computing resources such as virtual servers, network connections, and raw storage?
questions.explanation: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) provides fundamental computing, network, and storage infrastructure on-demand over the internet (e.g., AWS EC2, Google Compute Engine).

questions.question: Google Docs and Microsoft Office 365 accessed directly through a web browser are examples of which cloud service model?
questions.explanation: SaaS delivers end-user software applications over the internet without requiring local installation or software maintenance by the client.

questions.question: What is an integrated software platform that unifies core business operations such as inventory, accounting, HR, and sales called?
questions.explanation: ERP systems integrate and streamline core business processes across departments into a centralized unified database.

questions.question: Which cloud deployment model combines both private and public clouds, allowing data and apps to be shared between them?
questions.explanation: A hybrid cloud integrates private on-premises infrastructure with public cloud services, offering greater flexibility and data deployment options.

questions.question: What is the deceptive practice of tricking individuals into revealing sensitive credentials via fraudulent emails or fake websites?
questions.explanation: Phishing is a social engineering cyber attack where attackers disguise themselves as trustworthy entities to steal passwords, credit card numbers, or PINs.

questions.question: Ethical hackers who legally test and identify security vulnerabilities in systems to strengthen defenses are known as:
questions.explanation: White hat hackers are certified security specialists who perform authorized penetration testing to find and patch system vulnerabilities.

questions.question: Copying and presenting another author's written words, research ideas, or creative work as one's own without attribution is called:
questions.explanation: Plagiarism involves the unethical appropriation of another person's intellectual work or words without giving proper credit or citation.

questions.question: Unauthorized duplicating, downloading, or commercial distributing of copyrighted software programs is termed:
questions.explanation: Software piracy violates copyright law by illegally copying, distributing, sharing, or selling proprietary software without valid licenses.

questions.question: The scientific discipline of identifying, preserving, recovering, analyzing, and presenting electronic evidence in a court of law is:
questions.explanation: Digital forensics is the specialized branch of forensic science focused on recovering and examining material found in digital devices related to cybercrime investigations.
